name: Anantara Bazaruto Island Resort
insider_take: Paradise found on Mozambique's pristine Bazaruto Island, where endless white sand dunes meet turquoise waters in complete barefoot luxury.
whats_special: This exclusive resort sits on Bazaruto Island, part of a protected marine national park home to the last population of dugongs (sea cows) in the Western Indian Ocean. The island's massive sand dunes shift with seasonal winds, creating an ever-changing landscape that resembles the Sahara meeting the sea. Traditional dhow boats are the primary transport, maintaining the island's timeless charm.
pro_tip: Book a sunset dhow cruise during whale season (June-November) when humpback whales migrate through these waters - you might spot mothers with calves in the shallow channels between islands.
dont_miss: The Two Mile Reef snorkeling expedition to see manta rays and whale sharks, or climbing the towering sand dunes for panoramic views of the archipelago. The resort's spa treatments using local marula oil are legendary, and dining on fresh lobster caught by local fishermen is unforgettable.
pros: Exclusive private island location in pristine Bazaruto Archipelago
Exceptional marine activities including dhow sailing and world-class diving
Luxurious beachfront villas with stunning ocean views
Authentic Mozambican cultural experiences and local cuisine
cons: Remote island location requires boat transfer
